name: audio.mix
title: Mix (tracks, buses, pan)
summary: Declarative track/bus mixer: places clips sample-accurately on tracks, sums them to an exact length, optional per-track fx, gain automation, level, sidechain and master stage, and an optional per-cue level table. Plain float sum by default.
description: Sums audio clips on named tracks to an exact length. Processing order: (1) track_defaults are merged under each track with the same name; (2) every clip's `at` or `land_at` and every automation point's `at` is resolved (seconds or a timespec against `timeline`), and a clip placed with `land_at` gets its real start, read offset and length; (3) each distinct (src, offset_s, duration_s, fx) is decoded once; (4) optional per-clip leveling; (5) per clip gain, linear fades, the pan law, then mix at its sample position; (6) track fx; (7) track gain_db; (8) optional track `automation` (a gain curve in dB, ramped linearly between its points); (9) optional track `level` (measured after the automation); (10) optional sidechains; (11) mute; (12) bus fx and gain, then the master sum = buses + tracks without a bus; (13) optional master fx/gain/loudness; (14) fit to N samples and write; (15) optional `cues` table, measured on the stems (the tracks after steps 6-10). N = round(duration_s*sample_rate) or the latest clip end. A clip is placed by its start (`at`) or by the moment its sound is heard (`land_at` with `onset_s`: the clip starts early by the lead-in before the onset, and its `duration_s` is counted from the onset). A clip that runs past N is cut at N (a fade-out ends at the cut); a warning names it, with the seconds cut, only when the cut-off part peaks above -50 dBFS after the clip gain, so a file that runs on into silence is not reported. Defaults are neutral: no ducking, no normalisation, no limiter, no automation, no cue table; the default output is 32-bit float WAV so a sum above 0 dBFS does not clip. Pan law: mono into stereo is equal-power. Pan 0 gives 0.7071 per channel (matching ffmpeg's mono upmix); stereo into stereo at pan 0 is the identity; into mono a stereo clip becomes (L+R)/2 and pan is ignored.

preset.description: Optional named mix preset; its settings are merged under this request (the request wins).

sample_rate.description: Mix sample rate in Hz. Default 48000.

duration_s.description: Exact output length in seconds (rounded to whole samples). Omit to use the end of the latest clip.

timeline.description: Optional timeline.json ref; enables string `at` timespecs (scene, cue, bar, beat).

track_defaults.description: Per-track-name settings merged UNDER each track with that name (the request's track wins). Presets use this.

tracks.description: Tracks to sum. Each track holds clips and is processed independently.

buses.description: Named sub-mixes. Tracks with `bus` sum here before the buses are summed into the master.

gain_db.description: Bus fader in dB, applied after the bus fx. Default 0.

fx.description: Optional ffmpeg -af chain applied to the summed bus (for example "volume=6dB").

sidechain.description: Optional sidechain compressors. Each one ducks `target` using `key` as the trigger. Omit for no ducking.

key.description: Track name whose signal triggers the compressor.

lookahead_s.description: Seconds the key is advanced to look ahead. Default 0.

master.description: Final stage. Absent, or neutral (no fx, gain_db 0, no loudness), means the mix is not touched.

loudness.description: Optional loudness target for the master stage.

method.description: How to reach the target: a measured gain plus limiter, or ffmpeg loudnorm. Default "gain+limiter".

lra.description: Loudness range target in LU (loudnorm). Default 11.

format.description: Output WAV encoding: 32-bit float (no clipping), 24-bit or 16-bit. Default "wav32f".

stems.description: Also write stems/<track>.wav (32-bit float) for every track, after its fx, gain_db, automation, level and sidechains and before the bus. Default false.

preview_mp3.description: Also write a 192 kbps preview.mp3. Default false.

cues.description: Optional per-cue level table: for every clip of `tracks`, the level of its track over the clip's window next to the level of `reference` over the same window, measured on the stems (after the track fx, gain_db, automation, level and sidechains). A level is the K-weighted loudness of the window without gating (BS.1770 weighting, in LUFS); ratio_db = level_db - reference_db, so a positive ratio means the cue sits over the reference. report.json gets `cues` (one row per clip: track, clip index, name, at, end, level_db, reference_db, ratio_db; null where a window is empty or silent; plus land_at, the mix time its onset is heard, for a clip placed with `land_at` or giving `onset_s`) and `cues_summary` (per track: clips, min, median and max ratio_db); the result gets `cues_summary`, and `cues` too when there are at most 100 rows. Omit for no table.

reference.description: Track to compare every cue against, usually the music. Must name a track.

tracks.description: Tracks whose clips get one row each, in this order. Omit for every track except the reference.

window.description: The window measured for each clip: "audible" is the heard part of the clip (cut at the mix end) without its leading and trailing parts more than 30 dB under the clip's own peak (after its gain and fades); "clip" is the whole heard part. Rows report the window as at/end in mix seconds, from the clip's real position however it was placed. Default "audible".

level.description: Loudness-relative track level, applied after the track fx, gain_db and automation (and measured after them).

lufs.description: Absolute target integrated LUFS for the track.

relative_to.description: Another track name to be measured against.

lu.description: Offset in LU from relative_to's level.

clipLeveling.description: Per-clip loudness levelling, applied before fades and pan.

to.description: Target: a LUFS number, or "median" to use the median of the non-silent clips. Default "median".

tolerance_lu.description: Clips already this close to the target get 0 dB. Default 0.75.

min_db.description: Lower clamp for a clip gain, in dB. Default -9.

max_db.description: Upper clamp for a clip gain, in dB. Default 6.

automationPoint.description: One point of a track's gain curve.

at.description: When: seconds (number) or a timespec string ("scene", "scene#cue.end", "bar:4") resolved against `timeline`, exactly like a clip's `at`.

gain_db.description: Track gain at this point in dB, added to gain_db (0 = unchanged; a large negative value such as -100 is silence in practice).

trackDefaults.description: Fields applied UNDER a track with this name (the request's track wins).

gain_db.description: Default track fader in dB for matching tracks.

fx.description: Default track ffmpeg -af chain for matching tracks.

bus.description: Default bus name for matching tracks.

level.description: Default loudness-relative level for matching tracks.

clip_leveling.description: Default per-clip loudness levelling for matching tracks.

src.description: Audio file to place: a workspace path, job:<id>/<output-path> or pin:<name>.

at.description: Where the clip starts (its first played sample): seconds (number) or a timespec string ("scene", "scene#cue.end", "bar:4") resolved against `timeline`. A clip gives `at` or `land_at`, never both and never neither.

land_at.description: Where the clip's onset is heard, given instead of `at`: seconds (number) or a timespec string resolved against `timeline` exactly like `at`. The clip starts at land_at - (onset_s - offset_s), so the source sample at `onset_s` falls on this time; without `onset_s` it behaves as `at`. `duration_s` is then counted from the onset. If that start would be before 0, the lead-in is trimmed (reading starts later in the source) so the onset still lands here, and a warning says so. If `offset_s` is after `onset_s`, the onset is not in the part played: the start of the played part lands here, and a warning says so. Fades keep their meaning: the fade-in starts at the clip's first played sample (before the onset), the fade-out ends at its last. A clip `fx` that changes timing (atempo, adelay) moves the onset and is not corrected for.

onset_s.description: Where the sound begins inside the source, in seconds from the start of the source file (not from `offset_s`): the `onset_s` that sfx.fetch and audio.process report. With `land_at` it is the sample that lands on that time. With `at` the clip is not moved; the onset time is only reported as `land_at` in the `cues` rows. Absent counts as 0.

offset_s.description: Seconds into the source to start reading. Default 0.

duration_s.description: Seconds of source to use. With `at` they are counted from the first played sample (`offset_s`). With `land_at` they are counted from the onset (how long the sound is heard from the moment it lands), and the lead-in played before the onset is added. Omit to use the rest of the source.

gain_db.description: Clip gain in dB, applied before fades and pan. Default 0.

pan.description: Stereo position, -1 hard left .. 1 hard right (balance for stereo, equal-power for mono into stereo). Default 0.

fade_in_s.description: Linear fade-in length in seconds. Default 0.

fade_out_s.description: Linear fade-out length in seconds. Default 0.

fx.description: Optional per-clip ffmpeg -af chain applied while decoding (for example "volume=-3dB"). Source filters such as movie are refused.

name.description: Optional label for the clip (informational; the rows of the `cues` table carry it).
Track name, unique per mix; used by bus, level, sidechain and stem file names.

gain_db.description: Track fader in dB, applied after the track fx. Default 0 (unity).

mute.description: When true the track is not summed into the mix (it can still key a sidechain). Default false.

fx.description: Optional ffmpeg -af chain applied to the whole track (for example "volume=6dB").

bus.description: Name of a declared bus to sum this track into instead of the master. Omit for the master.

automation.description: Optional gain automation for the whole track, applied after the track fx and gain_db and before `level` and sidechains. Points {at, gain_db}: between two points the gain ramps linearly in dB, before the first point it holds the first value and after the last point the last value. Points out of time order are sorted (with a warning); two points at the same time make a step; one point is a constant gain. Omit for none.

level.description: Optional loudness-relative level for this track.

clip_leveling.description: Optional per-clip loudness levelling for this track.

clips.description: Clips placed on this track. May be empty.

examples.title: Two sine clips on one track
Dialogue over music (two tracks, fixed length)
Gain automation: the music dips 12 dB for a middle section, with ramps in and out
Per-cue level table: where each sound effect sits against the music
Land a sound on a moment: the hit starts 0.25 s into its file and is heard at 1.0 s for 0.2 s
